mechanisms.name: Root CA key stability (mesh-root-ca under the new `rotationPolicy` default)
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: The overlay pin is what prevents that.
resourcesConsumers: checkout (verifies ledger against its Secret's ca.crt)
mechanisms.mechanism: If the root key rotated, a leaf renewed against the new root would no longer verify against the stale `ca.crt` held by the peer, and mTLS would fail. The base file has no rotationPolicy, so removing or breaking the prod patch would silently turn rotation on for the CA.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The prod patch for `mesh-root-ca` keeps `Never`. When the root renews (1y duration, 720h renewBefore), it re-signs with the same key and the same subject, so every issued leaf and every `ca.crt` copy stays valid across a root renewal. The effective policy after the upgrade is **Never** (unchanged).
citedEvidence: rendered/manifest.diff: CRD description for spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy changes from "Default is `Never`" to "Default is `Always`", gate `DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways`
overlays/prod/mesh-root-ca-prod.yaml (sets rotationPolicy; the value is stored redacted; the comment says the digest is of "Never")
assumptions: The pinned value was taken as `Never` from the in-file comment. That is not a direct read of the value, which the repo stores redacted.
This is a static review of the repo, the rendered diff and the upstream notes. Nothing was run against a cluster.
missingEvidence: A live check that the root CA's rotationPolicy is `Never`
A rendered kustomize build of the prod overlay showing the merged object
A root renewal rehearsal confirming the public key stays the same
recommendedValidation: `kubectl get certificate -n cert-manager mesh-root-ca -o jsonpath='{.spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy}'` must print `Never`
Render `kustomize build platform/pki/overlays/prod` and confirm the merged object keeps `isCA`, `commonName`, `secretName` and `rotationPolicy: Never` together
Force-renew `mesh-root-ca` in staging with `Never` and confirm the public key is identical and leaves/peers still verify
Add `rotationPolicy: Never` to the root CA in the base `mesh-root-ca.yaml` as well as the overlay

mechanisms.name: Leaf key rotation versus the mTLS trust model
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: A new leaf key signed by the same CA is accepted by the peer.
mechanisms.mechanism: Under the new default `Always`, the leaf certificates get a new private key, which could break peers that pin the key.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Trust is by CA signature plus SANs. Nothing pins a leaf public key, hash or SPKI: there is no pinning in nginx or curl, no key-hash config, and no other consumer of these Secrets in `env/`.
citedEvidence: No pinning in nginx or curl, no key-hash config, no other consumer of these Secrets in `env/`
No other Certificate objects exist in `env/`
assumptions: This is a static review only. Nothing was run against a cluster.
missingEvidence: Any key-pinning or other consumers of the Secrets outside the repo
recommendedValidation: Staging rehearsal on v1.18.0: run `cmctl renew ledger-tls checkout-tls -n payments`, confirm the key fingerprint changes (`openssl pkey -pubout`) while `ca.crt` stays the same, and confirm `checkout` to `ledger` still succeeds

mechanisms.name: No immediate reissue on upgrade
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: Existing Secrets are not touched when the controller restarts or the CRD is updated.
mechanisms.mechanism: `rotationPolicy` applies only when a re-issuance happens. The first new-key issuance happens at the next renewal (720h duration, renewBefore 240h, so about 20 days after each cert's last issuance). A manual `cmctl renew` or any spec change that triggers reissue would also cause it.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Existing Secrets are not touched when the controller restarts or the CRD is updated.
missingEvidence: When each leaf was last issued
recommendedValidation: Record when each leaf was last issued so the first key rotation can be observed (about day 20 of each cycle), not discovered during an incident

mechanisms.name: Key parameters, and other CRD changes in the diff
mechanisms.mechanism: Key algorithm and size could change, and the other CRD changes in the diff (`signatureAlgorithm`, `revisionHistoryLimit` default 1, short names, ACME `profile`, Vault `serverName`, RBAC split of the challenges ClusterRole) could touch these resources.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Both leaves specify ECDSA/256, and the policy only controls whether a new key is generated, so the algorithm and size are unchanged. The other CRD changes do not touch these resources.
citedEvidence: rendered/manifest.diff (signatureAlgorithm, revisionHistoryLimit default 1, short names, ACME profile, Vault serverName, RBAC split of the challenges ClusterRole)

mechanisms.name: Leaf key now changes on each renewal (intended upstream behavior)
mechanisms.mechanism: With the default gate `DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways` on, `ledger-tls` and `checkout-tls` will generate a new private key at every renewal. The Secret's `tls.key` and `tls.crt` are replaced together.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Kubelet updates secret volumes atomically via symlink swap, so a file-level key/cert mismatch is unlikely. This is intended upstream behavior, and the assessment found no breakage.
citedEvidence: Controller args in the render (`--v=2`, `--cluster-resource-namespace`, ...) carry no feature-gate flag
assumptions: The gate is on by default here, inferred from the values file and the rendered args, not from the live controller
missingEvidence: A live check that the gate is not overridden in the running controller args
recommendedValidation: Confirm the running controller args have no `--feature-gates` flags that differ from the values file
Add an explicit `rotationPolicy: Always` to `ledger-tls` and `checkout-tls` if key rotation is wanted

mechanisms.name: `ledger` (nginx, 2 replicas in prod) does not hot-reload
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: This is **pre-existing** and not caused by the policy change
mechanisms.mechanism: nginx reads `/tls/tls.crt` and `/tls/tls.key` at startup and has no reload sidecar or reloader annotation. After a renewal, running workers keep serving the old cert and key pair. What the upgrade changes: the stale pair can no longer be assumed to share a key with the on-disk files, so any ad hoc process that mixes old in-memory state with new files has no shared key to fall back on. The real hazard is unchanged by this upgrade: the cert expires in nginx memory if no pod restarts within 30 days.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The old pair is self-consistent and stays valid until the old cert expires (30 days). A restart, scale-up or worker reload after a renewal picks up the new key and cert together, which is fine. With `Never`, the cert would still have been stale in memory.
citedEvidence: No reload sidecar or reloader annotation
missingEvidence: How `ledger` pods behave after the cert changes, both with no restart and after a rollout
recommendedValidation: In staging, confirm `ledger` pods behave as expected after the cert changes, both with no restart (still serving the old pair) and after a rollout
Fix the expiry-in-memory hazard separately, for example with a reloader or a restart on Secret change

mechanisms.name: `checkout` (curl loop) re-reads files on each iteration
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: After the upgrade the mismatch becomes possible (negligible, and self-healing).
mechanisms.mechanism: checkout picks up new material within about 30s of the Secret update. There is a small theoretical window where `tls.crt` and `tls.key` are read across a swap and do not match, giving one failed call. Today this is rare because the key never changes, so cert and key cannot be mismatched.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The risk is negligible and self-healing: it heals on the next iteration.
citedEvidence: checkout re-reads the files on each iteration
recommendedValidation: In staging, confirm `checkout` to `ledger` still succeeds after `cmctl renew`

mechanisms.mechanism: External consumers that depend on the leaf keys (pinned keys, allowlists, fingerprint monitors, backup, Vault sync) would see the key change at each renewal.

citedEvidence: ORIENTATION (the repo is the complete declaration)
assumptions: The repo is the complete declaration, per ORIENTATION

recommendedValidation: Take an inventory outside the repo of other consumers of the Secrets, key-pinning, and monitors keyed on key fingerprints or alerting on Secret changes

mechanisms.name: Timing of the next renewal against the 1.19 deadline
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: Nothing in this repo indicates that need.
mechanisms.mechanism: In 1.19 the gate goes GA and cannot be disabled. If anyone actually needs `Never` on the leaves, they must set it explicitly before then.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Nothing in this repo indicates a need for `Never` on the leaves.
recommendedValidation: Do not set `config.featureGates.DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false`. It would only delay the change to 1.19.

overall.recommendation: Proceed with conditions. The default change does not break this environment as declared, but it does change behavior. Before the upgrade, confirm the root CA's `Never` pin on the live cluster. Make the policy explicit: set `Never` in both the base and the overlay for the root CA, and set `Always` on the leaves if rotation is wanted. Do not disable the feature gate. The runtime checks (live checks, staging rehearsals, inventory outside the repo) are still open.
overall.quote: The default change does not break this environment as declared, but it does change behavior.
